content: In France, the social security system ensures that both prenatal and postnatal care in public hospitals is fully financed. Women who earn wages receive up to 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily payments ranging from €9,29 to €84,90, dependent on their prior earnings. Financially, pregnancy and the time around childbirth do not introduce new burdens; low-income families continue to face their usual challenges, while wealthier families maintain their standard of living. However, support for new mothers in terms of personnel help post-childbirth is lacking; paternity leave is capped at just 11 days, insufficient for a mother’s recovery postpartum. New mothers must navigate their recovery while managing the constant needs of their newborn, in addition to arranging for child care amid inadequate state-sponsored options, particularly in and around Paris. The cost of childcare is highly variable. In public daycare facilities, poorer families might manage an annual expense of about €1,000, but availability is scarce with only one slot for every eight infants. Consequently, many opt for private childcare solutions like childminders or nanny services. Any other questions?
